apologia-church-mesa.assessment: Apologia Church under Jeff Durbin is one of the sharpest, most unapologetically Reformed and culturally engaged churches in America. Durbin combines expository preaching with presuppositional apologetics (Van Til/Bahnsen tradition), aggressive anti-abortion street ministry, and public debate against secularism and LGBTQ ideology. Apologia Studios is a major media platform. The church is small but punches far above its weight in cultural impact. GREEN across the board — this is exactly the kind of muscular, doctrine-driven, mission-active church MOOP celebrates.

score_notes.christology: Christ alone. Presuppositional apologetics places Christ as Lord over all knowledge and reasoning.
score_notes.scripture: Inerrancy affirmed without compromise. Scripture is the self-attesting Word of God — ultimate authority.
score_notes.gender: Patriarchal. Durbin holds firmly to male headship in home and church. No women in pastoral or elder roles.
score_notes.leadership: Homepage identity focuses on mission/ministries; specific elder board and Durbin's role not detailed on home landing — prior research retained.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed soteriology (doctrines of grace). Justification by faith alone. Clear gospel preaching.
score_notes.cultural: Durbin is one of the most culturally engaged pastors in America — active in anti-abortion ministry outside clinics, fights LGBTQ ideology, opposes CRT. Unapologetically counter-cultural.
score_notes.preaching: Expository with strong apologetic application. Apologia Studios extends teaching reach globally via podcast and YouTube.
score_notes.mission: Homepage confirms End Abortion Now national campaign, Red Door Ministry abortion-clinic outreach, and Apologia Studios gospel-centered media — highly active evangelism and cultural engagement verified.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Strong emphasis on men leading families. Church culture is distinctly masculine and confrontational (in the best sense).
score_notes.denominational: Reformed Baptist — confessional accountability with elder governance.

apostles-anglican-knoxville-tn-acna.assessment: Apostles Anglican Church in west Knoxville is an ACNA parish in the Anglican Diocese of the South, led by Rector Rev. Jack King — who also serves as Dean of the Tennessee Convocation (ADOTS). He has been rector for over 13 years, providing mature pastoral leadership. The church is known for its 'scruffy hospitality' ethos and has been profiled in ACNA communications. The parish maintains one of the richest liturgical rhythms profiled here: Sunday services at 8:45 AM (with choral music), 11:15 AM (with acoustic music), plus 10:10 Formation Hour; Monday-Thursday daily Morning Prayer (8:30 AM), Midday Prayer (noon), and Evening Prayer (4:00 PM); and a Wednesday Noon Eucharist with Healing Service. Three strategic priorities include becoming a mother church, deepening spiritual formation across all ages, and serving the local neighborhood. ACNA 39 Articles framework with male-only ordination. Strong green-rated Anglican option for the Knoxville metro.
